Every request takes the same six steps.

Ask, plan, check, book, pay, record. The same loop under a Friday dinner and a payroll run, and a receipt at the end of each.

  1. Event

    Something happened: a message, a delivery on a channel, a schedule, a read from a connected tool.

    "Dinner on Friday with new people?"

  2. Fact

    What is known, with its source, who may see it, how long it holds and who consented. A change is a new row; the past stays.

    New in town, free on Friday evenings, open to meetups.

  3. Goal

    What a person or a company wants: a kind, a window, a place band, a budget band and a result that can be checked.

    Six people and a table, Friday evening, under 200k each.

  4. Plan and route

    Steps, and for each step a route: a model, a connected tool, the browser, a person inside the organisation, a person outside, a partner, or a call you consented to.

    Invite people open to meetups; ask a restaurant for a table.

  5. Proposal

    The one unit of action, between people and assistants alike. It is approved, run automatically under a policy you can read, or refused.

    "Table for six at 19:30, 150k each. Accept?"

  6. Receipt

    The verified outcome, and the only measure of success: what was asked, who did it, what it cost. It is what a profile shows.

    Dinner for 6, 900,000, split six ways.

Money rides the same path

Money follows the same path. The person who asks pays. A hold is placed at the route, released when the outcome is verified, and a bill can be split on the receipt. Budgets slow the assistant down before they stop it.

Channels are doors

Channels are doors into the first step. A request can arrive by web, WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, email, LINE, WeChat, SMS, Lark, Teams, Messenger or voice; which of these are open today is on each scenario page.

Every combination, the same six steps

Who it is about, what starts it, how a step is done, how it is checked, who pays and who sees it. Change a cell and the loop stays the same.

Axes and the values each can take
Subjectperson, workspace (personal or organisation), organisation unit (nested), installation
Triggera person's message, a channel delivery, a schedule, a goal, a connector read
Routemodel, cascade, connector piece, browser operator with handover, person inside (chain, pool role), person outside (service bank), partner, consented call
Verifierchecker, connected data (sheet, CRM, CI), a person, attendance, an external published result, a signed receipt
Payerthe asker, the workspace, a sponsor grant, a split, a hold, a room allowance
Audienceme, my workspace, friends, everyone (the same mask on every surface)
Channel in/outweb, WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, email, LINE, WeChat, SMS, Lark, Teams, Messenger and Instagram, voice

Fourteen scenarios

The tag on each scenario is read from our feature tracker when the site is built. Built means every part it needs is built. Partly built means some are. Coming means most are not yet, and the page says so in the future tense.

Partly built

Food and beverage owner, revenue goal

You will set a revenue goal and your assistant will run the plan, hand steps to your salespeople and report the result from your own sheet.

 Partly built

Language teacher and the pupils

A teacher will be found on the directory, parents will get a room per pupil, and progress will arrive as receipts.

 Partly built

Hyrox training group

A goal with a window will find your training partners, open a group room and bring in a coach on a split bill.

 Partly built

Small law firm

A client will write on WhatsApp, book a consult, and a licensed person will deliver the work with the money held until it is verified.

 Partly built

Find a rental

Your assistant will search listings, call landlords with your consent and bring you viewings to decide.

 Partly built

Hiring intro

You will ask for a hire, your network will vouch, and a trial task will prove the fit before anyone is committed.

 Partly built

Open-source maintainers

A review room will recommend reviewers from their skills and history, and continuous integration will be the checker.

 Partly built

Family care circle

A members-only room will share tasks with an escalation ladder, book a clinic by a consented call and split the bill.

 Partly built

Neighbourhood errand

A small errand will be posted with a hold and an acceptance window; a neighbour will take it, and there will never be a fee on free work.

 Partly built

Corporate group with subsidiaries

A parent will set policies and budgets by unit; subsidiaries will inherit narrower rules; receipts will roll up the chain.

 Partly built

Self-hosted installation in a hub room

Your own installation will join a hub room as a linked guest, and its receipts will be signed and checkable anywhere.

 Partly built

Affinity run club, where lawful

A host will set a lawful filter, take RSVPs up to a cap, split the bill and count attendance as proof.

 Partly built

A partner rents GPU nodes to a room pool

A partner will list a node for a room's pool; the served-by line will name it and the earnings will go to payouts.

 Built

E-commerce support

Customers write on Instagram or WhatsApp, the assistant answers within what it may share, and a refund is an approve-only proposal.

 Built

The ask card

A room publishes its bot-drafted ask under the owner's exposure; the right helpers find it by match, and the help ends in a receipt on both profiles.
